slides.title: The Continuum Beyond Approval
bullets: Clinical development doesn't stop at regulatory approval
It runs from first-in-human studies to years post-launch
MSLs need the full picture, not just the pivotal trials
An evidence-generation view lets you place any new study in context

slides.title: Reducing Risk Before Scaling Up
bullets: Phase I and II generate initial safety and tolerability data
Small, tightly controlled studies with preliminary efficacy signals
Their job is to de-risk before larger investment
Phase III delivers the confirmatory, pivotal evidence behind approval

slides.title: The Evidence That Fills Your Day
bullets: Phase IIIb studies start around or after pivotal completion
They explore new populations, comparators, and secondary endpoints
Phase IV, post-marketing, answers real-practice questions
Together they generate much of an MSL's daily evidence

slides.title: A Cycle, Not a Finish Line
bullets: Phase IV findings spark new research questions
These feed subgroup analyses, extension studies, new trials
Knowing the cycle helps you set honest expectations
It explains why some subgroup questions still lack answers

slides.title: Pragmatic and Adaptive Trials
bullets: Pragmatic trials mimic real practice while staying randomized
Broader inclusion criteria and non-specialist centers
Adaptive trials adjust dose, sample size, or criteria mid-study
Adaptive designs speed development without sacrificing rigor

slides.title: Mastering the Full Map
bullets: Knowing the full development trajectory builds real credibility
Lets you contextualize any new publication for an HCP
Goes beyond repeating the latest study's headline data

takeaway.title: Clinical development is a continuum MSLs must map end to end, not just the pivotal trials
bullets: Phase IIIb and IV generate the evidence MSLs use most
The cycle never stops — each phase raises new questions
Pragmatic and adaptive designs are increasingly part of that map
